transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been feeling a little, um, wound up lately? I hope I'm explaining this right. It’s just that I feel like I’m constantly running on a motor. I teach special education, so I’m used to being busy and having a lot of energy, which is usually a good thing, right? The kids definitely keep me on my toes. 

But lately, it's like I finish one thing at school, or even when I get home, and I just immediately jump right into the next task. I never seem to be able to just... shut myself off. I mean, I like being productive, and I don't want to complain, but I worry it's getting a bit exhausting. Does that make sense as a reason to come in?

You mentioned feeling like you're constantly running on a motor lately. Has this feeling of being wound up and jumping from task to task been happening most of the time over the past few weeks, or is this something new and different from how you normally feel?

Oh, um, that's a really good question. I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is... but, well, it's actually been a bit longer than a few weeks. I'd say this... this level of just constantly going, it's been happening for about eight months now? 

Yeah, right around eight months. That's, um, that's when an older relative of ours moved in with us. Which is wonderful, of course, I'm really glad we can help out family! I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about them at all, family is so important. It's just... I guess having them there maybe kicked my motor into an even higher gear, if that makes sense? 

I hope it's okay that I brought that up, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. Does that sound like a normal reaction to having a full house?

During these eight months when you've been feeling wound up and constantly going, how much sleep have you been getting each night, and do you feel like you need less sleep than usual, or are you just not taking the time to sleep because you're so busy?

Oh, sleep... right. Um, well, I hope I don't sound like I'm neglecting my health or anything. I really do try to take good care of myself so I can be there for my students and my family. 

But, honestly? I haven't really noticed a huge change in how much I sleep, or feeling like I don't need it. I mean, I'm definitely busy, and maybe I stay up a little later grading papers or helping out around the house, but... I don't think I'm sleeping significantly less than I used to. Or, at least, it doesn't feel like I'm running on empty because I'm skipping sleep, if that makes sense? 

I just... I don't think I've really paid that much attention to it, to be perfectly honest. I hope that's an okay answer. Should I be tracking my sleep more closely? I can definitely start doing that if it would be helpful for you!

When you say you feel wound up and constantly running on a motor, are you also experiencing a lot of worry or anxious thoughts about things, or is it more just a physical feeling of restlessness and difficulty slowing down without the worried thoughts?

Oh, um... anxious thoughts? I don't... I don't think so? I mean, I worry a little bit, like anyone would, right? You know, making sure the kids have what they need for school, or making sure dinner is ready on time... just normal everyday things. I hope I don't sound like a worrywart! 

But, um, it's not like my mind is spinning with bad thoughts or anything like that. It really is just... like my body can't stop moving. It's more of a physical thing, like I just have to keep doing something, anything, to burn off this energy. Even when I sit down to watch TV, my leg is bouncing or I'm fiddling with the remote. 

I really try to be positive and not let things get to me, so I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right. It's just hard to turn the physical engine off, even when my brain feels totally fine.

You mentioned that your relative moved in about eight months ago, which is when this feeling of being wound up started. Before that time, did you feel more relaxed and able to slow down, or were you already feeling this constant need to keep moving and stay busy?

Oh... um. Well, I really don't want to make it sound like my relative moving in caused all this. I'd hate for you to think I'm blaming them! To be perfectly honest... and I hope this doesn't make me sound like I was a badly behaved kid or anything... but I've actually kind of always been like this? 

Even way back in elementary school, my mother—bless her—she used to joke that I practically taught the class from my seat. I was just... always popping out of my chair, or talking, or maybe cutting in a little before the teacher even finished giving directions. I guess I was just really eager, you know? 

So, um, yeah, this... this need to keep moving, it's really been a part of who I am long before adulthood. It definitely didn't just start with this recent family change, it just maybe got a little more noticeable lately. I hope it's okay that I clarify that! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. Is that the kind of background information you were looking for?

How much is this constant need to keep moving and stay busy affecting your ability to do your job, your relationships, or your daily life? Would you say it's causing you significant problems, or is it mostly manageable?

Oh, um... well, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee or a bad partner. I really, really try my best to be helpful to everyone, I promise. But... I guess it is causing some, um, some bumps in the road lately. 

At work, you know, I love my students, but... well, the complaints from some of the other staff have gotten a little... serious. They actually put me on a, um, a corrective plan recently. I guess my energy is just a bit much for the classroom environment sometimes. And at home... my spouse has mentioned that the caregiving routines for our relative are actually harder now. They said they feel like they have to manage my energy on top of everything else we're dealing with. 

I just... I feel awful about it. I feel like I'm damaging the trust I have with my colleagues and my family, even though my intentions are good and I'm really just trying to help out. I hope you don't think less of me for admitting that. It's just... it's been really hard to hear that I'm making things worse when I want to make them better. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's a lot to unload.

You mentioned that as a child you would pop out of your seat and cut in before the teacher finished speaking. Even now, do you find that you have difficulty waiting your turn, or that you interrupt people when they're talking—or is it more that you just have lots of energy and restlessness?

Oh, gosh... um. I really hope this doesn't make me sound rude. I pride myself on being polite, I really do. But... well, yes, I suppose I do still have some trouble with that. 

I just... I get so eager to help out. Like, if my colleagues or the parents at school are discussing something, or even if my spouse is talking with our relative at home... I find myself just jumping right into the middle of their conversations. In my head, I really think I’m just being helpful and offering a solution, but... well, I guess I end up talking over them. Or I just kind of take charge before they’ve even had a chance to finish what they were saying. 

I feel awful when I realize I've done it, because I really don't mean to interrupt or make anyone feel unheard. I just get too enthusiastic to pitch in, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too pushy or overbearing. I really am just trying to be a team player!
